Overview

ERP Integration at AtherIQ

ERP systems are usually the most reliable data source a business has and the hardest one to reach. Stock, pricing, customers, invoices and production status are all in there — while the website, the CRM and the mobile app run on stale copies typed in by hand.

We build the integration layer between the ERP and everything around it. That means agreeing which system owns which record, choosing between real-time APIs and scheduled synchronisation for each data flow, and handling the failure cases properly so a network blip does not corrupt a stock figure.

We work with published ERP APIs and connectors where they exist, and with database-level or file-based exchange where a legacy or heavily customised ERP leaves no other option.

Talk it through first

Bring the problem rather than a specification. We will tell you what the work involves, where the risk sits and roughly what it costs before you commit to anything.

What we provide

Included in This Service

The concrete deliverables. Where something is out of scope for your budget, we say so before the quotation rather than after.

Integration architecture

A documented map of data flows, ownership, direction, frequency and failure handling before a line of integration code is written.

ERP to e-commerce

Products, pricing, stock, customers and orders synchronised between the ERP and your storefront in both directions.

ERP to CRM

Account, order and invoice history surfaced in the CRM so sales conversations reflect the real commercial position.

Middleware & API layer

A service layer that isolates other systems from ERP specifics, so future changes do not ripple across every application.

Scheduled & event-driven sync

Real-time webhooks where immediacy matters, batch jobs where it does not, with monitoring on both.

Data reconciliation & logging

Audit logs, reconciliation reports and alerting so discrepancies surface immediately instead of at month end.

Business benefits

Why It Matters Commercially

Outcomes rather than a restatement of the feature list.

One version of the numbers

Stock, pricing and order status are the same wherever anyone looks, because they come from the same place.

Manual re-keying stops

Faster order-to-fulfilment

Orders land in the ERP as they are placed rather than in an end-of-day batch typed in by someone.

Change without a rebuild

An integration layer means replacing a front end or a CRM later does not mean rebuilding every connection.

Questions

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you integrate ERP with our website or application?

Yes. We connect ERP systems to websites, e-commerce platforms, mobile apps, CRM and internal tools, using the ERP's API where one is available and database or file-based exchange where it is not.

Our ERP is old and heavily customised. Is integration still possible?

Usually. Older systems often lack a modern API, but there is almost always a supported route — a database view, a staging table, scheduled file exchange or a vendor connector. We assess the options before quoting.

Should data sync in real time or on a schedule?

It depends on the data. Stock and order status usually justify near real-time. Master data such as product catalogues is often fine on a scheduled sync. We decide flow by flow rather than applying one rule to everything.

How do you avoid breaking the ERP?

Integrations are read-heavy by default, write operations are scoped narrowly and tested in a non-production environment first, and rate limiting protects the ERP from load it was not sized for.

Ready to scope it?

Send us what you have — a brief, a wireframe, a spreadsheet of the current process, or just a description of what is not working.
